entry.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core version 31.3 introduces a range of bug fixes and performance enhancements, along with updated translations to improve user accessibility across different languages. Users are encouraged to report any issues they encounter via the official [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues).
For those upgrading from an older release, it is essential to fully shut down the current instance before proceeding. On Windows, this involves running the installer, while on macOS users should overwrite `/Applications/Bitcoin-Qt`, and Linux users need to update the `bin/` and `libexec/` directories. Upgrading from versions that have reached end-of-life remains feasible, although the process may be prolonged if data directory migration is required. Compatibility with older wallet formats is generally maintained, ensuring continuity for long-term users.
The software supports and is rigorously tested on Linux Kernel 3.17 and newer, macOS 14, and Windows 10 (version 1903) or later. While Bitcoin Core is expected to function on other Unix-like systems, these platforms do not receive the same level of testing and support, making them less suitable for production use.
Several significant updates are included in this release. In networking, transaction inventory messages now process only unique transactions, as detailed in pull request [#35878](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35878), which contributes to enhanced efficiency. Continuous integration improvements feature inline runner selection ([#35441](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35441)) and the adoption of the warp docker buildkit cache ([#35571](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35571)), which streamline the development pipeline.
Appreciation is extended to all direct contributors, notably Greg Sanders and willcl-ark, as well as to community members who assisted with translation efforts. The collaborative contributions ensure ongoing refinement and stability of Bitcoin Core.
